summary: # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Pleating Classroom - Currently Updated to P5 p04 4_Pullback ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore how to manipulate wrinkles in fabric using the brush tool in Marvelous Designer. This guide will cover the use of brush size, gradient effects, and negative values to achieve desired pleating effects on garments. ## Using the Brush Tool To reduce or increase the wrinkle effect in a specific area, you can utilize the brush tool. ### Brush Size and Gradient Effect The size of the brush corresponds to the area you are working on. The center of the brush features a gradient effect, where the center part holds the highest value, and it gradually disperses outward. This allows you to control the gradient area by adjusting the gradient value. - **Action:** Click and drag the mouse to draw the curve area along the desired section. - **Observation:** After opening the simulation, you will notice that the brush is now positioned correctly. ## Observing Wrinkle Formation Once the simulation runs, you will see various irregular wrinkles in the specified area. ### Irregular Wrinkles When the brush is applied in certain areas, particularly in the middle of the board, it will also create irregular wrinkles. ## Utilizing Negative Values Next, we will examine the application of negative values in wrinkle management. ### Negative Shrink Rate By employing a negative shrink rate, you can partially flatten wrinkles because the grid is shrunk. However, it's important to note that this method does not universally apply to all wrinkles on the board. - **Limitations:** Although the middle part may exhibit a shrink rate, the stretching of the grid can lead to increased wrinkles on either side. Therefore, using this technique over a large area is not recommended. ### Application in Skirt-Like Wrinkles When addressing skirt-like wrinkles, it is advisable to apply negative values specifically in the middle of the board. - **Example:** In skirts designed to tighten the waist and body, the negative value of the grid can help flatten the edges. - **Caution:** If the shrink rate is excessively high, it may result in overly tight areas despite only minimal adjustments to the grid. ## Conclusion In summary, the use of the brush tool and negative values in Marvelous Designer can significantly affect the appearance of wrinkles in fabric. It is best to apply these techniques with caution and precision to avoid unwanted tightness or irregularities in the garment's design.
